record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can one prove exponential spatial decay of localized solutions for a general class of nonlinear equations and time-dependent potentials, beyond known pointwise decay in dimensions five and higher and known smoothness or boundedness of all powers of the dilation operator A in some purely nonlinear dispersive settings?

evidence.quote: Problem 1- Exponential Decay of Localized Solutions Can one prove exponential decay of the localized solutions of a general class of nonlinear equations and time dependent potentials? We have already shown that in 5 or more dimensions the solutions have some pointwise decay in x. We also know, quite generally that Anψ is uniformly bounded in L2 for all n for purely nonlinear equations (e.g. Inter-critical in 3 or more dimensions) and that the solution is smooth.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider nonlinear dispersive equations of the form
$$ i\partial_t \psi = -\Delta \psi + V(t,x)\psi + N(\psi), \qquad x \in \mathbb{R}^d, \; t \in \mathbb{R}, $$
where $V(t,x)$ is a (sufficiently regular) time-dependent real-valued potential and $N$ is a nonlinear term (for instance a power nonlinearity $N(\psi) = \mu |\psi|^{p-1}\psi$ in an inter-critical regime when $d \ge 3$). Let $A = \tfrac{1}{2}(x \cdot \nabla + \nabla \cdot x)$ denote the generator of dilations on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$.

Call a global solution $\psi(t,\cdot) \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ "localized" if it remains in a compact subset of $L^2$ for all time (equivalently, it does not radiate to spatial infinity). Assume the following are already known under suitable hypotheses:
(a) for $d \ge 5$, every localized solution exhibits some pointwise spatial decay in $x$;
(b) for purely nonlinear inter-critical equations in $d \ge 3$, the iterates $A^n \psi$ are uniformly bounded in $L^2$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and $\psi(t,\cdot)$ is smooth.

Question: Establish, for a general class of such nonlinear equations (possibly including time-dependent potentials $V(t,x)$), the exponential spatial decay of every localized solution, i.e. prove the existence of constants $C, \alpha > 0$ such that
$$ |\psi(t,x)| \le C e^{-\alpha |x|} \quad \text{for all } t \in \mathbb{R},\, x \in \mathbb{R}^d, $$
or determine the largest class of equations and potentials for which this exponential decay holds.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a 2024 review on scattering theory of linear and nonlinear waves. No subsequent literature located so far establishes exponential spatial decay of localized solutions at this level of generality; partial results give only pointwise polynomial-type decay (in dimensions $\ge 5$) and smoothness/$L^2$-boundedness of dilation powers in purely nonlinear inter-critical settings.
